message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | What | How it works | |------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you agree on). Points come from the cards left in opponents’ hands when someone goes “UNO.” | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (red, yellow, green, blue) × 25 cards each (1–9, two of each; plus two “Skip,” “Reverse,” and “Draw Two” per color). 4 “Wild” and 4 “Wild Draw Four.” | | **Setup** | Shuffle, deal 7 cards to each player. Place the rest face‑down as the draw pile; flip the top card to start the discard pile. | | **Turn** | 1️⃣ Play one card that matches either the color or the number/symbol of the top discard.
2️⃣ If you have no playable card, draw one from the draw pile. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately. | | **Special Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – changes direction of play.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and skips their turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and skips their turn (must be played only if you have no matching color). | | **Calling UNO** | When you’re down to your last card, shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | First player to get rid of all cards wins the round. Score points based on the cards remaining in opponents’ hands: numbers = face value, Skip/Reverse/Draw Two = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50. | | **Game End** | First player to reach the agreed point total (commonly 500) wins the game. | That’s the core of Uno—fast, colorful, and full of strategy!
